messages:
sasha: @channel :rotating_light: CS ticket 98214 — customer (ACME) reporting intermittent 503s during long streaming toolcalls in eu-west-1. Observed upstream inference worker exit (container restart) with SIGSEGV and PTX invalid-memory-access patterns. Need triage; impact: several requests/timeouts and customer-visible latency spikes.
kevin: Any repro steps or model details? batch sizes, streaming toggles, pool id?
sasha: Model: rwd-llm-3b-quant (hosted), streaming=true, batch_size=1, avg seq len ~2048 tokens. Happens when toolcall triggers heavy KV-prefetch. Pool id: pool-37. QPS spike ≈120 rps for that pool at time of failure. Crash snippet below.
```
[2026-03-17T14:08:21Z] worker-upstream[pid=4213]: free(): invalid pointer
[2026-03-17T14:08:21Z] gpu0: cuLaunchKernel -> CudaErrorInvalidDeviceMemory
[2026-03-17T14:08:21Z] infer: runtime aborting due to uncaught SIGSEGV
stack:
  lm_infer()+0x1a3f
  kv_prefetch()+0x4b2
  cuLaunchKernel(...) -> invalid device address
```
eng-runtime: paste the full container stdout / coredump if available. Also which GPU driver version on the host? This reads like a PTX/device mismatch or memory corruption.
maria: This pattern is reminiscent of the kernel-race we saw previously when prefetch and dynamic model swap coincide — large kv allocations + fragmented device memory -> invalid launches. Quick mitigation: disable KV_PREFETCH on that pool and reduce prefetch window.
sasha: oncall-bot created incident INC-2026-98214 and assigned to eng-runtime. Customer notified we are investigating; they asked for ETA and whether they should switch to a fallback model.
oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-98214 created by sasha, severity: p1, channel: incidents.
cs-agent: CS note: customer asked about credits for failed API calls and timeout billing. Advised temporary credits pending RCA, will hold formal ask until we confirm root cause.
kevin: rolling change now — disabling KV_PREFETCH for pool-37 and setting PREFETCH_WINDOW=256 as a canary. Will watch error rate and p95.
eng-runtime: quick analysis: host driver moved to 536.12 in eu-west-1 two days ago; runtime compiled PTX might not be compatible with new driver for one kernel path used by kv prefetch. Also suspect fragmentation: per-request kv cache ~1.2GB allocated transiently for these long contexts. If driver rejects kernel parameters it can manifest as invalid device memory errors and then segfault on free().
maria: mitigation checklist: 1) disable prefetch for pool-37; 2) lower PREFETCH_WINDOW to 256 tokens globally for streaming pools until patch; 3) pin GPU driver to 535.x for recently updated hosts or roll runtime PTX forward.
kevin: applied changes at 14:12Z (PREFETCH=false for pool-37, PREFETCH_WINDOW=256). Observability shows immediate drop in 503s and p95 returned to baseline within 10m. No new SIGSEGVs recorded for 20m.
sasha: CS notified customer of temporary mitigation and that we will scope a rollback/driver pin or runtime patch. Customer willing to accept short failover; wants follow-up RCA and ETA for permanent fix.
eng-runtime: next steps: reproduce in staging with driver 536.x and same model/config, capture nvprof / cupti traces, produce minimal repro harness that triggers invalid launch. Add runtime guard to detect PTX launch failures and fail request gracefully instead of crashing the process. I'll open infra tickets and a runtime PR.
maria: long-term: add prefetch backpressure (circuit-breaker on per-request kv allocation) and a migration test matrix for driver/kernel compatibility on release.
sasha: thanks team — monitoring for 30m then will update CS. If anything new appears ping me directly. :thumbsup:
